decision.rationale: Lire la source intégrée la plus rapide mesurée avant de sélectionner une transformation d’assemblage; l’exécution est correcte et a obtenu 0,00456 s.
Examiner le changement réel de répartition par lignes avant de décider s’il est compatible avec le candidat SIMD persistant mesuré le plus rapide.

Partir de Gm1, le meilleur candidat correct mesuré (0,00456 s). Tester uniquement son interaction avec le partage cyclique des lignes `schedule(static,1)` de T1; conserver le noyau `omp simd`, l’équipe persistante, les barrières et l’alternance des buffers de Gm1. La source T1 seule étant plus lente, ne pas reprendre son noyau comme amélioration présumée; garder Gm1 comme référence.
Lire la source SIMD T2 la plus rapide mesurée avant de choisir une autre intégration; le premier essai de partage par lignes est correct mais plus lent que Gm1.

Use the correct, fastest measured base d60. Test only whether T2's restrict-qualified stencil pointers improve optimization in that base; do not repeat the prior slower cyclic row schedule. The candidate will require correctness and timing verification before it can replace d60.

Gm1 plus T2's restrict qualifiers is correct and measures 0.004548 s, a small improvement over Gm1's 0.004556 s; the row-schedule integration was slower at 0.006401 s. Before deciding whether another integration is worthwhile, inspect T2's valid explicit eight-lane SIMD source as a contrasting idea; no gain is assumed.

Keep c10a as the fastest correct measured base (0.004548 s). Test T2's explicit eight-lane vector kernel with its complete vector blocks and scalar tail while retaining c10a's persistent OpenMP team, static-z worksharing, timestep barriers, restrict qualifiers, and buffer alternation. The standalone vector candidate was correct but slower than T2's omp simd variant, so any benefit in this threaded integration remains unproven; retain c10a as fallback.

Stop further integration experiments: c10a remains the fastest correct measured candidate at 0.004548 s. The explicit-vector integration measured 0.004888 s and the cyclic-row integration 0.006401 s; neither improved on c10a. The small difference between c10a and Gm1 (0.004556 s) is not independent confirmation, so the controller should select among verified candidates and perform the required final confirmation.

children.objective: Isolate the benefit of CPU worksharing across stencil rows or planes, using the run-time threads argument as the thread budget. Consider a persistent OpenMP parallel region around the six steps to avoid repeated team-startup overhead, while retaining the required global synchronization between steps and even/odd buffer semantics. Include initialization only if measurements justify it. Validate and compare repeated results at both sizes and both thread budgets; do not combine this track with temporal fusion or a new SIMD kernel.
children.subject: OpenMP worksharing and persistent stencil-step region

children.objective: Using the existing compiler configuration, first determine whether GCC already vectorizes the contiguous-x loop, then compare compiler-directed vectorization with an explicit SIMD implementation if appropriate. Handle all interior bounds and tails for every valid size, preserve results within tolerance, and do not change compiler options or restructure threading or timesteps. Compare correctness and repeated timings at every official size/thread combination.
children.subject: GCC SIMD effectiveness in the single-step x kernel

children.objective: Investigate spatial tiling across the six timesteps to reuse intermediate values and reduce full-volume traffic. Account for radius-three dependencies at each step, alternating buffers, and the initialized values of fixed boundary regions. The complete output must still contain both specified buffers with the correct final interior values and preserved boundaries; scratch-allocation cost is timed. Support every valid input size and compare correctness and repeated timings at every official size/thread combination.
